data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism asserts that 'the "fittest" (most tested) theories are the only ones available for further mutation and testing.' This is both factually false about science and breaks the very analogy it relies on. In biological evolution, extinct lineages cannot be revived — differential survival is a genuine constraint on what can subsequently mutate. In science, refuted or poorly-tested theories remain perpetually available for revival and modification (e.g., Lamarckian inheritance re-emerged with epigenetics; Einstein revived and modified Mach's relationalism). The word 'only' imposes a closure condition on the space of testable theories that has no analog in the actual practice of science and no analog in the biological mechanism it invokes. Furthermore, the claim conflates an evaluative standard (corroboration — a logical relation between theory and surviving tests) with a causal mechanism (the sociological processes — peer review, funding, training — that actually cause theory selection). In biology, fitness is not the causal mechanism either; mutation, inheritance, and differential reproduction are. Calling corroboration itself the 'causal mechanism' commits the same category error as calling fitness the causal mechanism of natural selection, stripping the analogy of its explanatory force.
